name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Auto-apply PR-Agent style and doc fixes to *all* PRs, but only if the PR-Agent score is 95% or higher. This cuts review time for the clearest fixes while keeping the 90% threshold as a backstop for riskier PRs. The trade-off is more false negatives—we’ll miss some safe fixes—but we avoid the bigger risk of normalizing sloppy reviews.

name: Gauge
text: PR-Agent’s 90% threshold still ignores *what* the tool flags—it could block a PR for a single low-risk typo while missing a real logic flaw. A better rule: auto-apply only to *unchanged* lines in PRs, where context is already locked, and let humans review *all* edits to existing code. Settle it by testing both rules on a week of PRs and comparing missed risks vs. false positives.
